To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of motor control exercises, in conjunction with a sling exercise, is more effective than general exercises in the treatment of chronic low back pain.
motor control exercises, sling exercise, and general exercises are equally effective at 3 months for patients with chronic nonspecific low back pain.
the motor control exercises were superior to the general exercises in reducing pain, disability, and fear avoidance beliefs at 3 months, but not at 12 months.

the current evidence supports the use of exercise therapy as an intervention in patients with low back pain, and that the most appropriate exercise is a supervised exercise program that includes a variety of exercises that address flexibility, strength, endurance, and coordination.

the motor control exercise group had the most significant improvement on the Oswestry Disability Index, the Roland Morris Questionnaire and on the pain scale, while the group receiving sling exercises had a more positive effect on the pain scale.

the use of a lumbar brace for the treatment of chronic low back pain is not effective.
motor control exercises, when compared to general exercises, are more effective in the short term for patients with chronic nonspecific low back pain.
the best exercise program for low back pain is a comprehensive one that addresses both motor control and general fitness.
